name: The minimum number of distinct distances determined by n points in the Euclidean plane.
comment: The Mathoverflow link has an image from page 200 of Brass reference.
reference: P. Brass, W. O. J. Moser and J. Pach, Research Problems in Discrete Geometry, Springer (2005), p. 200.
link: Paul Erdős, On sets of distances of n points, American Mathematical Monthly 53, pp. 248-250 (1946).
Paul Erdős and Peter Fishburn, Maximum planar sets that determine k distances, Discrete Math. 160 (1996), 115-125.
Erdős problems database contributors, Erdős problem database, see no. 89.
Larry Guth and Nets Hawk Katz, On the Erdős distinct distance problem in the plane, arXiv:1011.4105 [math.CO], 2010-2011.
Larry Guth and Nets Hawk Katz, On the Erdős distinct distances problem in the plane, Ann. of Math., 181 (2015), pp. 155-190.
Roger Mansuy, Le problème des distances d'Erdős, Mathematik Park, Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris, 2013.
formula: a(n) <= C * n / (log n)^(1/2) for some constant C [Erdős, 1946].
a(n) >= C * n / (log n) for some constant C [Guth and Katz, 2015]. (End)
example: a(4) = a(5) = 2 from the 2 distinct distances between vertices of a square and a regular pentagon.
author: _Michael Somos_, Feb 25 2011
